title: Exton Square Mall plan cleared in court, with construction eyed for summer 2027
summary: After a Nov. 13 ruling overturned West Whiteland's rejection, Abrams Realty says it will push ahead on Exton Town Centre: 381 apartments, 172 townhomes and 165 active-adult units around a green boulevard, with Boscov's and Round1 staying. Township supervisors were set to weigh an appeal Nov. 24.

title: West Chester kicks off holiday shopping weekends with deals and free parking
summary: Starting Black Friday, most of the borough's 180 independent shops and restaurants offer 20 to 30 percent discounts and spend-and-save deals under more than 100,000 lights. Street parking is free Nov. 27 to 29, and carolers roam the shopping district.

title: Deer trapped behind Randolph Woods fence stir up Malvern residents
summary: The fence Malvern put up last December to let its 43-acre preserve regrow has deer stuck inside, and residents asked council to remove it. The borough says vandals are cutting holes and propping gates open, and has added cameras.

title: Caln Township takes ownership of the 1726 Caln Meetinghouse
summary: The township celebrated taking over the 300-year-old Quaker meetinghouse, its graveyard and 5.9 acres of open space, and has pledged long-term upkeep. Quaker members had approached the township about the transfer in 2025.

title: Judge pauses demolition of West Goshen's Forsythe Farm if residents post $25,000
summary: A Commonwealth Court judge halted the teardown of the vacant fieldstone farmhouse at 905 Westtown Road while Save Forsythe Farm appeals, but only if the group files a $25,000 bond by Nov. 30. Supporters had raised just over $7,000 as of Monday.

title: Kimberton Whole Foods will move its Downingtown store to River Station
summary: The grocer plans a larger store in the River Station redevelopment at Route 322 and Boot Road by fall 2028, about half a mile from its Milltown Shopping Center location, which stays open until then. It is a relocation, not a second Downingtown store.

title: West Chester Borough Council advances a 12.6% property tax increase
summary: Council voted 4-3 to move the 2027 increase forward, which works out to roughly $178 more a year on a $174,600 assessment. Officials point to rising emergency medical costs and shifting stormwater costs into the general fund; a final vote is set for Dec. 16.

title: Safe Harbor looks for sponsors for its remaining shelter beds by Dec. 1
summary: West Chester's Safe Harbor is asking businesses and neighbors to sponsor its 40 emergency beds at $1,000 each through Dec. 1. It is the only shelter in the county that takes single women.
loc: Safe Harbor of Chester County, West Chester

title: DEP plans winter air tests at homes near the Bishop Tube site in Frazer
summary: New groundwater samples found cancer-causing solvents east of the former steel tubing plant on Malin Road at higher levels than expected, so the state wants 24-hour indoor air monitoring at about two dozen nearby properties, including 14 new ones. Testing depends on owners agreeing to it.

title: Chester County proposes a 5.29% property tax increase for 2027
summary: Commissioners introduced a preliminary $782.2 million budget on Nov. 18 that would add about $27.30 a year per $100,000 of assessed value, after last year's budget held the rate flat. The final vote is set for Dec. 16 at 10 a.m. at the county building on West Market Street.

title: Hometown Christmas Parade returns Dec. 4 with more marching bands
summary: The chamber's parade steps off at 7 p.m. Friday, Dec. 4, after a 6:30 p.m. lighting of the 28-foot tree at the Historic Chester County Courthouse. Organizers added marching bands this year, and float competitions return.
loc: High and Market streets, West Chester

title: Kennett Community Grocer opens Nov. 23 in the old Minnie's Bakery
summary: Kennett Square's member-owned food co-op, eight years in the making, opens Monday at Minnie's Square with goods from more than 125 local farms and makers. The group signed its lease a year ago and has passed 500 member households.
